html:
Basil I was Byzantine emperor from 867 to 886 and founder of the Macedonian dynasty, which ruled for nearly two hundred years. Born to a peasant family of Armenian descent in the theme of Macedonia, in Thrace, he came to Constantinople as a groom known for his strength and his way with horses.

He won the favour of Emperor Michael III, who made him chamberlain, had him marry the emperor's own mistress, and in 866 crowned him co-emperor. Basil had already killed Michael's uncle Bardas, the real power at court. In 867 he had Michael murdered and ruled alone.

As emperor he proved capable. He deposed Photios to please Rome but later brought him back, began the revision of Roman law that his son Leo VI finished as the Basilika, and fought the Arabs in the east and in southern Italy. His dynasty presided over a revival of learning and the conquests of Basil II. He died after a hunting accident in 886.
